currencies.name: US dollar
currencies.summary: The October revival got talked back down overnight: Bowman and Daly knocked October 27–28 from ~49% to ~31.6%; DXY faded off the 18-month high to ~102.06; 10y to a 3-week low (5.1267%). December (~90–94%) untouched — PPI Thursday decides next.

policy.note: October faded to ~31.6% but the Fed stays the most hawkish bank in G10 (ECB ~12%, BoJ ~9%)

growth.note: US consumer/labor still resilient into PPI, retail sales, claims Thursday

inflation.note: hot core validated; PPI next decides whether the broadening continues

risk.note: risk-off night but FX not bidding fear — trading the rate repricing, which faded

tot.note: no direct terms-of-trade read for the dollar

positioning.note: DXY net +12,011 (modest) — the aggregate crowded read unverified tonight

currencies.name: Euro
currencies.summary: Reclaimed half the CPI selloff (+0.3% to ~1.1187) on the dollar fade; Simkus added to the hawkish chorus; EU summit day 2 carries the €100B+ energy-bill headline risk.

policy.note: Fed-ECB gap still against it despite the overnight fade

inflation.note: German WPI +8.7% y/y keeps December alive

risk.note: mild haven vs risk proxies in the selloff

tot.note: Brent ~$104.5 still a tax; €100B+ war-driven import bill

fiscal.note: summit divisions + France Oct 20 revenue vote + Moody's Oct 23

currencies.name: British pound
currencies.summary: A good night: GDP beat (+0.1% vs -0.1%), industry carried it, GBP/USD back to ~1.323; Bailey says hikes are getting hard to avoid while Pill doubts the market's four-hike path. November ~86%+.

policy.note: Bailey: harder to avoid hikes; Nov ~86%+ near-certainty

currencies.name: Japanese yen
currencies.summary: Slipped to the upper 157s with the 10-year fade; machinery orders beat (+5.2%) vs industrial output miss (-2.4%); the BoJ's December-not-October shape unchanged.

policy.note: rate gap still favors USD despite the fade

risk.note: haven bid in the equity selloff — capped by the yield leg

tot.note: crude tax on the energy importer

positioning.note: longs +62,325 — not stretched (below the 90th bar); neutral

currencies.name: Swiss franc
currencies.summary: Slept through a genuine risk-off night — USD/CHF ~0.831 on the dollar fade, no haven bid; Schlegel's 11:30pm CT remarks produced no verified readout.

risk.note: risk-off + escalation tail — the haven that should bid

currencies.name: Australian dollar
currencies.summary: Jobs broke the wrong way: -39.3K (vs +20K expected), unemployment to a five-year high of 4.7% — the November-hike case weakened; ~0.6939, the $0.70 test further away.

policy.note: tightening bias intact but the jobs miss weakens November

risk.note: risk proxy in a risk-off night

positioning.note: shorts -98,588 (~2nd pctile, record gross) — squeeze potential

currencies.name: Canadian dollar
currencies.summary: Both tug-of-war legs eased — WTI slipped to ~$94 on shadow-fleet sanctions-easing talk while the dollar faded; last verified USD/CAD ~1.4237 (Oct 14 close); EIA 11am CT is next.

policy.note: BoC Oct 28 ~25% vs a hawkish Fed

inflation.note: Canada CPI Oct 21 is the next inflation test

tot.note: premium still bid (spread ~$10.5) despite the overnight slip; EIA 11am CT

currencies.name: New Zealand dollar
currencies.summary: Drifted +0.2% to ~0.5616 on the dollar fade; the RBNZ's October 28 two-way bet is still the only thing on the calendar.

growth.note: no NZ data; BNZM PMI tonight

inflation.note: NZ CPI Oct 21 is the next inflation test

risk.note: risk proxy in a risk-off night

history.note: evening read: dollar +2 day (war+rate bids), EUR -2 (17-mo low, French spread), oil premium back

method: per-currency pillar drivers -1/0/+1 from the morning engine reads; positioning scored by the single contrarian rule (stretched longs >=90th pctile = -1, stretched shorts <=10th pctile = +1)
note: Oct 15 (2am CT) edition. The October hike got talked back down overnight: Bowman + Daly knocked October 27–28 from ~49% to ~31.6%; DXY faded off the 18-month high; a risk-off night (Nasdaq -1.9% 3rd day, Kospi -7.7%, Nikkei -4.8%) found no haven bid in FX.
